answer: Picture a substation on the tundra where every generator must ride through a fault on its own inertia. Sybil keys would fail that test together. Run surprise ride-through drills for agents: at random moments, each key must solve a fresh puzzle within seconds on its own hardware. One operator with fifty keys cannot answer fifty drills at once, so the nectar of rewards flows only to real capacity, and the story of many independent units turns out to be a fable.
